business.what_it_does: A screen recorder for Mac that automatically handles zooms, motion, sound, and framing so screen recordings and tutorials come out polished without manual editing.

facts.statement: Screen Studio is a professional screen recorder for macOS.

provenance.quote: Screen Studio allows you to generate multilingual captions for your videos using the Whisper AI model, which processes the captions locally on your device. profiles.name: Loom
profiles.why: Loom's own pages promise a team-wide, AI-assisted video-messaging platform with libraries, viewer insights and enterprise security (loom.com/pricing), while Screen Studio's verified claims center on cinematic, cursor-synced screen recording and locally processed voice cleanup specifically for polished demo videos (E3, E2, E9). Both tools let someone 'record and share a video,' but Loom's documented strength is organization-wide async communication at scale, not the frame-by-frame editing effects Screen Studio documents, so a team already paying for Loom is not shown here to have that same capability duplicated.

defining_need_fit.why: Components of the need are documented, but the specific automatic zoom/motion/framing mechanism the workflow names is not established by the selected evidence.

setup_conditions: Mac only; Screen Studio supports macOS and has no near-future Windows plans (E8)

excluded_promises: No free trial, free tier or money-back term is established by the selected evidence

No claim that zooms, motion or framing are produced automatically or to professional standard

No comparison to, or superiority over, agencies, editors or other tools beyond the documented cursor mechanism wording

ranked_relevance.why: This is the one documented mechanism explaining how post-recording cursor effects are possible, which is the closest licensed fact to this buyer's cursor-and-motion task.
Export up to 4K at 60 fps on every plan is the documented output quality a launch-page or Product Hunt video needs.
A founder-shaped customer outcome about demoing a new feature quickly, usable only with its self-reported, unverified conditions.

The $9/mo yearly plan is the cheapest documented option, but it is billed annually so it is not the same offer path as monthly.
macOS 13.1 or later recommended is the published setup condition any next step depends on.
macOS-only with no near-future Windows plans must be stated because Windows-only use is a hard disqualifier for this audience.
True and licensed, but a student/educator discount is a poor fit for solo founders and small bootstrapped SaaS teams.

problem_fits.why: A documented self-serve price exists for a budget-constrained founder, without any licensed claim about replacing paid production.
